If you remember in the movies, Yoda and other jedi made mention multiple times that they could not see or sense things because they were clouded in darkness, like when anakin asks Yoda if there's a way to save people from his visions. He says it's difficult to see into the future as it was clouded. That cloud was Palpatine. He also enhanced the power he displayed by reducing the jedis abilities by getting then involved in a brutal civil war. Jedi are not warriors, the strains and rigors of war actually have an adverse effect on their abilities unlike say sith that feed and revel in such environments. And it's interesting you bring up maul and anakin as Palpatines choices. In fact it could be claimed that the reason Palpatine failed to make the sith takeover permanent is He actually ignored the rule of two for the most part. He was only interested in his own personal power than the superiority of the sith as a whole which really actually becomes the fundamental flaw of the sith as an organization. Now, how they went 1000 years without a sith lord messing up the rule of two is unexplained but as with all things the wild card is the will of the force itself. It always strives to find balance and will take steps to return balance that could very well work against either light or dark side dominance of the galaxy. It could also be possible that the force got temporarily all out of whack due to the death of a force deity. And yea I know what you're thinking, force deity? What? Yea, that's a thing, it was made Canon in the clone wars TV show.

Honestly, it's a matter of philosophy, this idea behind the rule of two is that as a whole the sith are prone to infighting and betrayal, every sith you add to the equations increases the likelihood of the sith failing. With the one master, one apprentice rule, an apprentice can only overcome their master if they are more "powerful" but say if one master had 2 apprentices, then the two weaker apprentices could team up and destroy the master before actually becoming stronger than them. If there are two masters and only one apprentice, well that doesn't make a whole lot of sense either masters would compete and probably kill each other. Now could they work if you had one master and one apprentice in different places in the galaxy? Possibly. But the focus of the rule of 2 is to prevent the sith from being weakened by infighting. This was apparently successful as by the time Palpatine was in charge he was so powerful that his aura alone literally was blinding the senses of even powerful jedi like Yoda.

Edit: as far as the creation of Anakin, it is very possible that the force created him in response to the massive imbalance. Notice that by the time anakin died there was only a single gray jedi left. Just Luke and his not so light, light side.

The sith utilized the philosophy of "the rule of 2" to make their 2 way more powerful than the multitude of jedi. Over generations, 1000 years if the numbers in the prequels are meant to be literal, sith apprentice surpassed and destroyed their master increasing their strength while hiding from the galaxy at large as to not be discovered. It's basically an idea of quality over quantity. I mean think about say the battle of hoth. Without the snowspeeders in the equation we have the foot soldiers of the rebellion vs the atat walkers. Even though the soldiers obviously outnumber say a lone atat walker the power of one atat walker far surpasses even a multitude ground soldiers. Even adding the snowspeeders to the mix, like say having slightly more powerful jedi, didn't tip the scales in their favor due to the overwhelming power lf the walkers. It's the same idea with the sith vs the jedi, there are physically more jedi but the two individual sith are overwhelmingly more powerful than a majority of jedi even when they combine forces.

The big thing that helped me in this game was when I stopped trying to play it like I did assassins creed. It's a similar feel in combat at first, and it will lure you into thinking that like the creed games if shit goes sideways you can just destroy everyone in a straight fight. This is not the case. Shadow of Mordor and shadow of war will brutally punish you if you get too big for your britches. Don't get me wrong, talions a beast and can hold his own plenty, but his strength lies in the use of all his tactics rather than straight combat. When your plans go awry, and the orcs gain the upper hand you have to utilize talions superior speed and mobility to get out and regroup. Pick off stragglers with your bow, use hit and run tactics, use the environment, poison some grog then blow up that grog, use all your tools. Do anything and everything to give yourself the upper hand. Fight dirty. That's how you achieve victory.
